title: Arrow Functions and Callbacks Check
description: Arrow syntax, implicit return, and callbacks with map/filter.

questions.explanation: `map` calls the arrow once per item. Expression-body `(n) => n * 2` returns each doubled value, so the array becomes `[2, 4, 6]`.
A block body `{ ... }` does not auto-return. Without `return`, the caller gets `undefined`. Use `(a, b) => a + b` or `return a + b` inside the block.
`inc` is a callback (a function value). `applyTwice` calls it twice: `5 → 6 → 7`.
`filter` keeps only scores `>= 60`. `map` builds a new array of labels — both use arrow callbacks.
Each element is clamped into `[0, 10]`: `-2 → 0`, `5` stays, `12 → 10`. The callback passed to `map` calls `clamp`.

questions.prompt: Why can you call a `function` declaration before its line in the file, but not a `const` arrow?

options.text: Function declarations are hoisted; `const` arrows are not available before their line

questions.explanation: Declarations are hoisted. An arrow assigned with `const` must be declared before you call it — declare helpers near the top.
